sentences.text: An ice cube is solid water. So why does it float on the very liquid it came from?
The trick is density: how much matter fits into a certain amount of space.
When water freezes, hydrogen bonds hold its molecules in a more open crystal structure, with more space between them.
The amount of water hasn't changed. But now it takes up more room, so its density drops.
In fact, fresh water expands by about nine percent when it freezes. Solid doesn't always mean more tightly packed.
That lower-density ice floats on the denser liquid water, though much of the ice stays underwater.
So, is your ice cube defying gravity, or just taking up extra space and refusing to leave?
